text: {"summary":"The Netflix picks are The Jungle Book, The Invitation, 13th, Norman Lear: Just Another Version of You, White Girl, Barry, Justin Timberlake + the Tennessee Kids, Zootopia, Under the Shadow (arriving January 9), The Little Prince, and Captain America: Civil War. Hulu’s pick is Tina Fey’s war-correspondent dramedy Whiskey Tango Foxtrot."}

{"summary":"Ratan Tata said he felt lonely and deeply hurt by newspaper attacks on his and Tata Group’s reputations amid the dispute with Cyrus Mistry. Speaking at a Tata Chemicals meeting called to remove Nusli Wadia from its board, he thanked shareholders for their overwhelming support and said truth would prevail."}

{"summary":"CBS canceled “We Are Men” after two episodes, with viewership falling from 6.4 million to 5.4 million. “2 Broke Girls” will take its 8:30 p.m. Monday slot starting October 14, while “Mike and Molly” returns November 4 at 9 p.m., following temporary “Big Bang Theory” repeats."}

{"summary":"Scientists worry Finding Dory will spark demand for pet blue tangs, just as Finding Nemo reportedly boosted clownfish sales by 40%. Unlike clownfish, blue tangs fare poorly in tanks, and increased collection from loosely regulated waters around Indonesia and the Philippines could damage wild populations and marine ecosystems."}

{"summary":"Fashion designer Charlotte Ronson’s New York City home is surprisingly comfortable and down-to-earth rather than lavish. White walls showcase eclectic artwork, while baby-blue dining chairs and fresh flowers add bright pops of color; Ronson says surrounding herself with art and beautiful things makes a difference."}

{"summary":"The author switched from a beloved Galaxy S7 to an iPhone 6s Plus because the iPhone lasted much longer on a charge despite having a smaller battery. Under heavy use, the S7 routinely died around 5 p.m., making battery endurance more important than its superior camera, design, and preferred Android software."}

{"summary":"Around 40 people were burned during a hot-coal walk at a Tony Robbins seminar in Dallas, possibly because they paused to take selfies—the “dumbest reason” teased by the post. Witnesses reported participants using phones; lingering increases heat exposure, whereas brief contact with low-conductivity coals can prevent burns."}

{"summary":"This curated list highlights 29 online works from 2016 about sexism, racism, sexual violence, politics and resilience, mixing reporting, personal essays, satire and fiction. Standouts include Emily Doe’s courtroom letter to Brock Turner, Roxane Gay’s “On Making Black Lives Matter,” Solange’s “And Do You Belong? I Do.” and Masha Gessen’s “Autocracy: Rules for Survival.”"}

{"summary":"The food industry plans to replace confusing food-label wording with clearer, easier-to-understand language at grocery stores nationwide. The article doesn’t specify which labels will change, what the new wording will be, or when it will appear."}

{"summary":"ScHoolboy Q revealed he nearly quit rap after Oxymoron because years of touring kept him away from his young daughter. He said he refused to put money and his career ahead of family, though he ultimately continued making music and released another album."}

{"summary":"Cinematographer Dean Cundey revealed that The Thing uses a subtle lighting cue to hint at who is human: a small gleam in the actors’ eyes gives them “life.” Its absence can suggest an alien imitation—a detail viewers can look for when revisiting the film’s ambiguous ending."}

{"summary":"Spark was New Zealand’s most complained-about company in the Commerce Commission’s 2016 Consumer Issues Paper, with 140 complaints, followed by Vodafone with 133 and Trade Me sellers with 121. The commission cautioned that complaints do not necessarily indicate lawbreaking; Spark said none of its complaints were taken forward."}

{"summary":"Primal Pit Paste CEO Amy Cazin turned down Wal-Mart’s offer to stock her natural deodorants because her young company couldn’t handle the retailer’s order volumes. Started with $100, the business generated over $800,000 in its first 18 months and later expanded into Whole Foods and thousands of independent retailers."}

{"summary":"The post rounds up 19 teens’ outrageous or memorable moments in 2016, including sending an umbrella photo in response to a shower-pic request, asking oneself to homecoming, befriending a deer, and making tiny pancakes for chickens. Other highlights include winning homecoming in a dinosaur costume and discovering a dead body while playing Pokémon Go."}

{"summary":"Men are using period-tracking apps such as iAmAMan and uPMS to monitor female colleagues’ and partners’ menstrual cycles, supposedly to avoid PMS-related moods and stay on their “good side.” The article describes one workplace where tracking began after an argument and notes public backlash over the practice."}

{"summary":"While riding near Little Rock, Arkansas, Bret and Zach Winingar found an emaciated dog locked in a chewed-up crate, barely able to stand. They rescued her, named her Charlie Bravo, and adopted her; donations covered her veterinary care, with the remainder earmarked for a charity called C.B.’s Angels."}

{"summary":"McLaren plans to spend £1 billion (about $1.45 billion) over six years to launch 15 new cars by 2022, including a P1 successor and an all-electric model. The investment will fund new powertrains, hybrids and carbon-fiber structures, with annual sales targeted to rise from 2,000 to 5,000 cars."}

{"summary":"Whole Foods co-CEO Walter Robb says he won’t hire candidates who display arrogance—specifically, a lack of humility and excessive self-promotion. The article advises balancing confidence with humility by acknowledging coworkers’ contributions and explaining how your skills can help others and the organization succeed."}

{"summary":"Home robots and smart appliances often offer too little benefit for the setup, maintenance, and supervision they require, while ordinary appliances already work well. Unlike controlled machines such as dishwashers, robots struggle with unpredictable homes—as illustrated by a Roomba spreading dog poop across its owner’s floors."}

{"summary":"The unusual morning drink is bone broth, made by simmering beef or chicken bones with vegetables, water and apple cider vinegar for 8–24 hours. The article touts it as a filling breakfast drink, citing wellness experts’ claims of benefits for bones, skin and digestion, and recommends using high-quality bones."}

{"summary":"Amateur archaeologists discovered an uncharted tunnel beneath Emperor Hadrian’s Villa in Tivoli, Italy, linking its Academy area to a 2.5-mile underground roadway. The wider network likely let slaves, merchants and supply carts service the estate out of sight, though the newly uncovered passage’s specific purpose remains unknown."}

{"summary":"Rockstar didn’t actually announce anything: the article is explicitly labeled satire, not genuine GTA 6 news. It jokes about predictable features such as playable characters, improved graphics, online multiplayer, mature content and expensive in-game purchases, while mocking release delays, server outages and fan expectations."}

{"summary":"The article’s “disturbing truth” is that the dramatic weight loss on NBC’s The Biggest Loser was apparently only temporary. It says contestants shed pounds by training eight hours a day, but provides no details or evidence about what happened afterward."}

{"summary":"The article says four-blade ceiling fans common in the US run more slowly and circulate air to supplement air conditioning, while three-blade fans common in India serve as stand-alone cooling appliances. It attributes the latter’s faster operation and greater energy efficiency to their lighter design."}

{"summary":"Jessica Simpson wore black skinny jeans, a low-cut top, a blazer and patent-leather stilettos to dinner at Sagebrush Cantina in Calabasas with fiancé Eric Johnson and daughter Maxwell, three months after welcoming son Ace. She also hinted at a return to recording by tweeting, “I need to make music.”"}

{"summary":"The Battlefield 1 open beta ends Thursday, September 8. A patch removes time limits from Sinai Desert Conquest matches, which now end when a team reaches 250 points, while planned server stress tests may cause downtime; the full game launches worldwide October 21."}

{"summary":"Leann surprised her Grandpa Ried with an ultrasound announcing her pregnancy, then revealed the real secret: she was expecting twins. He cried with joy upon learning he would become a great-grandfather, and Leann later gave birth to twin girls in February 2016."}

{"summary":"The thing being teased is close, supportive relationships—not wealth, fame or career success. Harvard’s 75-plus-year study found that men with satisfying, stable relationships were happier and healthier as they aged, while unwanted isolation was associated with earlier physical and cognitive decline and shorter lives."}

{"summary":"Saudi Arabia bought the most U.S.-made weapons in 2011–2015, followed by the United Arab Emirates, Turkey, South Korea, Australia, Taiwan, India, Singapore, Iraq and Egypt, according to SIPRI. The U.S. supplied nearly one-third of global arms exports, with about 40% of its exports going to the Middle East."}

{"summary":"Tesla’s surprises include hidden Rainbow Road, rainbow charging-port, James Bond submarine and Mars-screen Easter eggs, plus model names intended to spell “S3XY.” The article also highlights plans for electric trucks and buses, the Model S breaking roof-crush testing equipment, its pioneering Motor Trend award and its 315-mile range."}

{"summary":"Nine-year-old Molly sang Kasey Chambers’ “Am I Not Pretty Enough?” during a blind audition on The Voice Kids Australia, prompting every judge to turn around. The teased response was Mel B praising Molly’s control and confidence, then urging her to choose her as coach with a “girl-to-girl” appeal."}

{"summary":"Bill Maher urged TV hosts interviewing Donald Trump to treat him as a politician: ask tough questions, hold him accountable and “don’t let him use you.” Speaking on “Jimmy Kimmel Live,” Maher also said he would welcome Trump onto his own show, “Real Time.”"}

{"summary":"The city was Sydney: LendLease sold all 391 apartments offered at its Darling Square development in just four hours on Saturday. Prices ranged from A$630,000 for a studio to A$3.5 million for a penthouse, showing strong inner-city demand despite concerns about looming apartment oversupply."}

{"summary":"BBC golf commentator Peter Alliss was caught on mic saying Sergio Garcia’s fiancée, Angela Akins, wore “the shortest skirt in the country” and adding, “There will be some fun in the hotel tonight!” after Garcia’s Masters win. The BBC said Alliss recognized his off-air skirt remark was inappropriate."}

{"summary":"Elizabeth Warren’s memoir, A Fighting Chance, pledges to do everything possible for struggling Americans and recounts repeatedly accepting public roles she initially resisted. The article argues that this pattern and her commitment to economic fairness make a case for seeking the presidency, despite her insistence she isn’t running."}

{"summary":"Lindsay Lohan is recording with Duran Duran, revealing the collaboration teased in the post. She shared an Instagram photo from the studio with her younger sister, singer Ali Lohan, and band members Simon Le Bon and Nick Rhodes, captioned “recording with some greats!!!”"}

{"summary":"The tiny plastic tripod in your pizza box is a “pizza saver”: it props up the cardboard lid so it doesn’t sag onto the pizza and pull off the cheese. Carmela Vitale designed it in 1983 and received a patent in 1985, though she apparently never manufactured it herself."}

{"summary":"The article predicts the 9-to-5 will fade as millennials demand flexible schedules for family and education, technology enables remote work, and companies cut office costs. It cites a survey finding 77% of millennials expect flexibility to improve productivity and a Chinese-firm study reporting 13% higher productivity among telecommuters."}

{"summary":"Alex Newell, who plays Wade “Unique” Adams on “Glee,” has joined the cast of “Geography Club,” a teen movie adapted from Brent Hartinger’s novel. Newell said the script appealed to him as an opportunity to open viewers’ eyes and show “what we go through.”"}

{"summary":"Drake’s “Views” became the first album to spend nine consecutive weeks atop the Billboard 200 with streaming accounting for a significant share of its sales. In its ninth week, nearly 100 million streams supplied about 77% of its album-equivalent sales, showing how streaming can sustain a blockbuster album."}

{"summary":"Research suggests people may come to look like their names: In experiments, volunteers shown a headshot and four or five possible names picked the correct name significantly more often than chance. The findings suggest a link between names and appearance, though the excerpt doesn’t explain what causes it."}

{"summary":"The article recommends 20 apps to encourage outdoor activities, including ViewRanger for hiking routes, Strava for running and cycling, Star Walk 2 for stargazing, Cachly for geocaching and Forest XPlorer for woodland visits. Other picks help find wildlife reserves, children’s activities, dog-friendly beaches, skateparks and campsites, or support fishing, drones and parkour."}

{"summary":"The article ranks the 2014–15 Knicks as New York sports’ second-worst disaster: at publication, they were 5–36 with 16 straight losses, worse than even the 1962 Mets. Only Columbia football’s 44-game losing streak from 1983–88 ranks worse, though it spanned multiple seasons."}

{"summary":"“Biggest Loser” host Bob Harper recommends intermittent fasting—his version involves skipping breakfast and eating within a 10-hour window—to help contestants counter reduced calorie burning after massive weight loss. Research suggests short-term weight-loss benefits, but long-term maintenance remains unproven, and fasting is unsuitable for some people with medical conditions."}

{"summary":"The teased #8 is KFC’s BBQ sandwich: an anonymous former employee alleges it uses stale chicken soaked in BBQ sauce and kept on a heater for a month. Other unverified employee anecdotes warn about dirty McCafé and slush machines, reheated theater popcorn, old hot dogs, and long-held nuggets and beans."}

{"summary":"The mystery celebrity wearing a Beatles-style mop-top wig is Alfred Hitchcock, not Moe Howard. The photo, reportedly taken in 1964, shows the “Psycho” director sporting the Fab Four’s signature hairstyle, though the article doesn’t explain why."}

{"summary":"Galbani’s string cheese packaging uses stereotypically male cartoon characters for its full-fat cheeses and female characters for reduced-fat versions. The article calls out this gendered marketing after a parent reported that their five-year-old daughter noticed the distinction and asked for the “girl cheese.”"}

{"summary":"Google’s secret car company is called Google Auto LLC, formed in 2011 to legally operate its self-driving car project and listed as the manufacturer of its 23 autonomous Lexus SUVs. Despite being licensed as an automaker in California, Google said it planned to seek established automakers as manufacturing partners."}

{"summary":"The teased rat catcher is Eranna, about 60, who lives near Denkanikottai, Tamil Nadu, and says he is the last traditional rat catcher in hundreds of nearby villages—not all India. He learned to smoke rats out of field burrows from his father and grandfather, eats his catches, and has no successor."}

{"summary":"The teased “brutal truth” is the author’s claim that businesses labeled pyramid schemes are actually legitimate multilevel marketing opportunities that work, especially for mothers seeking income from home. The article champions sellers’ hard work and urges readers to support them, but offers no concrete earnings data to substantiate its claims."}

{"summary":"A couple in Gujarat agreed to family planning only after having 17 children—16 daughters and one son—because the father kept hoping for another boy. Village elders persuaded them to stop expanding their family, which struggled financially, and the mother underwent a tubectomy."}

{"summary":"Bill Carter, The New York Times’ television reporter for more than 25 years and author of The Late Shift, is taking a voluntary buyout. He called leaving agonizing but said the generous severance created economic pressure to accept; he is seeking another job and has a new late-night television book contract."}

{"summary":"Comparing prices of the same foods across countries—Big Macs, Starbucks lattes, pizza, wings and Nobu’s miso black cod—offers a playful gauge of currencies’ purchasing power. Results vary by dish: latte prices suggest the dollar is 25% overvalued against the pound, while pizza prices suggest the pound is 26% overvalued against the dollar."}

{"summary":"An Orphan Black blooper reel released by BBC America for Comic-Con shows Tatiana Maslany mixing up her characters: while playing Cosima in a phone scene, she tells the person on the other end they need to talk to Cosima—accidentally referring to her own character as someone else."}

{"summary":"You generally don’t need to fast before a cholesterol test: eating has little clinically meaningful effect on LDL, HDL or total cholesterol results. Fasting may improve triglyceride measurement accuracy, but while U.S. guidelines cited in the article still prefer fasting, several European guidelines no longer routinely require it."}

{"summary":"The rescued “cats” were actually baby genets, abandoned after children throwing rocks scared away their mother in South Africa. At Daktari Wildlife Orphanage, a dog named Candy adopted them and unexpectedly began producing milk despite not being pregnant; two eventually returned to the wild, while one stayed at the center."}

{"summary":"No—the spectator at Mike Tyson’s 1995 fight wasn’t a time traveler holding a camera phone; the device could have been a contemporary handheld camera, such as a Casio QV-10A or Logitech Fotoman. The article explains how modern assumptions can make ordinary objects in old footage seem anachronistic."}

{"summary":"Syracuse University tops GrubHub’s late-night ordering rankings across more than 350 college campuses, with one in four student orders placed between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. Overall, college students are 87% more likely than the average diner to order late-night meals and spend about 10% less per meal."}

{"summary":"The phone teased is the Turing Phone Cadenza, a concept unveiled by California-based Turing Robotic Industries—not an available product. Its claimed specifications include 12GB RAM, 1TB storage, two Snapdragon 830 processors, a 60MP camera with 6K recording, four SIM slots and AI-enabled Swordfish OS, with release projected for the following year."}

{"summary":"Matt Mager found his wife Dayna asleep in their baby Luella’s crib because she had climbed in to comfort her crying daughter. Dayna committed to responding whenever Luella cried after hearing a missionary’s story about silent babies in a Ugandan orphanage, though the article omits the orphanage worker’s explanation."}

{"summary":"The article’s 10 low-effort suggestions are to cut sugary juice, improve posture, practice calming breathing, garden, stretch for 10 minutes daily, try a flotation tank, walk, avoid suppressing sneezes, limit distressing Twitter use, and drink warm water. Its claims about warm water’s benefits and equivalence to exercise are unsupported exaggerations."}

{"summary":"The new candy is M&M’s Mega, an oversized version with three times the chocolate of regular M&M’s, available in original milk chocolate and peanut varieties. Launching in May 2014, it will cost $1.49 for a small milk-chocolate bag or $3.29 for a medium bag of either variety."}

{"summary":"A Lovehoney survey of 4,400 customers found sex lasted an average of 19 minutes, including 10 minutes of foreplay—leaving about nine minutes for intercourse. Just over half were satisfied, though the sample of sex-toy customers may not represent the general population."}

{"summary":"“The Newsroom” actress Alison Pill told Conan O’Brien she accidentally tweeted a topless selfie because she didn’t realize her new BlackBerry had a touchscreen. She quickly deleted the photo, which she had kept while away from then-fiancé Jay Baruchel, and described the mistake as “hideously embarrassing.”"}

{"summary":"The USDA approved four Chinese processors to export cooked poultry from U.S.-raised birds, meaning chicken nuggets could be processed in China without origin labeling or on-site USDA inspectors. Critics cite China’s food-safety problems and fear future rules could allow imports of chickens raised and slaughtered there, too."}

{"summary":"Nintendo’s $60 NES Classic Edition is permanently limited to its 30 built-in games: you can’t add more through downloads, cartridges or external storage. Its cartridge slot is decorative, and it has no internet connectivity, making it a standalone nostalgia device rather than an expandable console."}

{"summary":"Adding milk to Coca-Cola produces visible changes within 15 minutes; after about an hour, a mostly clear liquid sits above clumps of curdled milk. The cola’s acidity causes milk proteins to coagulate and settle, but this striking experiment does not itself demonstrate the bodily harm the article suggests."}

{"summary":"After someone burned an American flag on Ben Schofield’s pickup at Wasatch High School in Utah, classmates extinguished the fire. The next day, several dozen students rallied wearing red, white and blue and flying American flags, while Schofield returned to school with a replacement flag on his truck."}

{"summary":"An Argentine farmer named Jose discovered a fossilized glyptodon shell on his property in Carlos Spegazzini, near Buenos Aires, on Christmas Day. At least 10,000 years old, the shell belonged to an extinct armored relative of the armadillo that could weigh up to two tons."}

{"summary":"Labrador retrievers were America’s most popular purebred dog in 2016, topping the American Kennel Club’s rankings for a record 26th consecutive year. Rottweilers rose to eighth, their highest position in nearly 20 years; the rankings cover AKC registrations, not mixed-breed dogs or designer hybrids."}

{"summary":"Michel Bechard was taken into police custody after stripping naked in front of a White House security gate on Friday. According to the Secret Service, he assaulted an officer as officers attempted to subdue him."}

{"summary":"Madden NFL 2016 predicts the Carolina Panthers will beat the Denver Broncos 24–20 in Super Bowl 50, with Cam Newton scoring the game-winning touchdown and earning MVP honors. The annual computer-controlled simulation had correctly picked nine of the previous 12 Super Bowl winners."}

{"summary":"Anthony pranked his 17-year-old sister Anelle by wearing a cap and gown to her high school graduation and sitting prominently in the family’s box seats. Having graduated just a year earlier, he was recognized by many classmates, leaving Anelle struggling to contain her laughter onstage."}

{"summary":"The leaves are bay leaves: the article recommends placing them around corners, kitchens, and gardens, preferably dried and crushed for a stronger scent. It claims their smell repels cockroaches, but provides no evidence that they eliminate infestations or guarantee you’ll never see cockroaches again."}

{"summary":"The “good” thing Texas did was reject Mary Lou Bruner, a State Board of Education candidate known for inflammatory Facebook posts and conspiracy theories, including claims about Obama and school shootings. Chiropractor and Lufkin school board president Kevin M. Ellis defeated her by a wide margin."}

{"summary":"A viral fan theory imagines Friends ending with Phoebe as a homeless meth user watching the other five friends at Central Perk, having imagined herself in their lives for all 10 seasons. It’s a fan’s dark alternate ending, not the show’s actual story."}

{"summary":"The FBI arrested a man suspected of spraying a mixture of hand cleaner, water and Tomcat mouse poison onto self-serve food bars and produce at a Whole Foods in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and targeting other grocery stores. Whole Foods discarded the food and sanitized the stations; no illnesses were reported."}

{"summary":"Researchers identified Tamu Massif beneath the northwest Pacific as a single enormous volcano, reported in the study as Earth's largest—not merely part of an oceanic plateau. About 400 miles wide and 2.5 miles tall, it formed roughly 144 million years ago and has long been extinct."}

{"summary":"To see 2014’s biggest supermoon, look for the full moon after sunset on Sunday, August 10; check the U.S. Naval Observatory website for local viewing times. The moon becomes full at 2:10 p.m. EDT, within the same hour it reaches its closest point to Earth."}

{"summary":"Cats don’t purr only when happy: purring may also signal hunger, anxiety or discomfort, or help them soothe themselves. The article suggests their 25–150 Hz vibrations might aid bone and muscle repair, but emphasizes that scientists still debate purring’s exact purposes."}

{"summary":"“Real Housewives” stars Adrienne Maloof and Paul Nassif have resolved all outstanding issues in their divorce settlement and pending litigation. The couple, who filed for divorce in August 2012, said they are moving forward as co-parents and prioritizing their three children’s well-being and privacy."}

{"summary":"Shailene Woodley’s apparent favorite word is “badass.” The article rounds up nine months of interviews in which the “Divergent” star repeatedly uses it to describe her character Tris, co-star Theo James, author Veronica Roth, her stunt double, and even the prospect of shaving her head."}

{"summary":"Legendary Simpsons writer John Swartzwelder is using Twitter to promote his books by posting funny excerpts rather than new jokes. The article jokingly suggests that this blatant self-promotion—delivering his signature dry humor while refusing to create original Twitter material—might itself be masterful comedy or performance art."}

{"summary":"March’s overlooked pop picks are The Drums’ “Blood Under My Belt,” Offaiah’s “Run,” Computer Games’ “Every Single Night,” Nelly Furtado’s “Phoenix,” Aminé’s “REDMERCEDES,” Maddie Ross’ “You’re Still My Sugar,” B.O.Y.’s “Winning,” Louis the Child featuring Ashe’s “World on Fire,” Steps’ “Scared of the Dark,” and TYSM’s “Wraith.”"}

{"summary":"BubblesDelFuego’s Fallout 4 world-record run, as reported in the article, finishes the game in just over an hour on “very easy” difficulty. It combines a sprint-focused character build with exploits—including wall clipping, teleporting cover slides and triggering a final quest early—to bypass travel and large portions of the story."}

{"summary":"Fitness instructor Siphiwe Baleka recommends six sleep habits to support metabolism and weight management: track sleep with a wearable, keep consistent bed and wake times, stop using electronics an hour before bed, keep devices out of the bedroom, drink chamomile tea, and read before sleep."}

{"summary":"The cylinder on your laptop charger cord is a ferrite bead, which filters high-frequency electromagnetic interference. It helps prevent the cable from acting like an antenna that picks up or broadcasts unwanted signals, reducing interference with nearby electronics."}

{"summary":"A preliminary study of nearly 26,000 men linked Viagra (sildenafil) use to a higher risk of melanoma, a potentially deadly skin cancer, with current users showing an 84% higher risk. The findings do not establish causation, and researchers said it was too early to change prescribing practices."}

{"summary":"Climate change is driving more polar bears to cannibalism: melting Arctic sea ice makes hunting seals harder, leading hungry adult males to prey on younger bears. The article describes National Geographic footage of a male chasing a mother and her cub before catching and eating the cub."}

{"summary":"Tesla’s “Master Plan, Part Deux” proposes expanding its electric lineup with a compact SUV, a pickup truck, a heavy-duty Tesla Semi and high-capacity urban transport vehicles. The latter two were targeted for 2017 debuts, while production upgrades would help Tesla build vehicles faster and more efficiently."}

{"summary":"Walter White will be appearing on billboards across Los Angeles as part of AMC’s Emmy campaign for “Breaking Bad”—not in new episodes. After winning Outstanding Drama Series the previous year, the show is seeking more awards for the final eight episodes of its fifth season."}

{"summary":"The post teases 23 tongue-in-cheek products for people who want to be left alone, including conversation-deterring clothing, antisocial pins and mugs, a bed tent, an ostrich pillow, and a giant plush cat body pillow. This affiliate shopping list also features solitude-themed socks, door decals, stationery, and prints of famous recluses."}

{"summary":"The article argues that an Apple–Tesla acquisition would founder on the clash between Tim Cook’s cautious, operations-focused leadership and Elon Musk’s independent, risk-taking ambitions. Despite apparent financial and strategic benefits, the author believes Musk would have to leave Tesla—and wouldn’t want to."}

{"summary":"Houston, Texas, is the city forecast to overtake Chicago as America’s third-largest, with the article projecting the shift within eight to 10 years. Energy-sector jobs, low taxes and migration have fueled Houston’s growth, though its dependence on oil, traffic congestion and air-quality problems pose challenges."}

{"summary":"At publication, the three longest flights by distance were Air India’s Delhi–San Francisco (9,400 miles, 14.5 hours), Emirates’ Dubai–Auckland (8,820 miles, over 17 hours), and Qantas’ Dallas–Sydney (8,577 miles, 16 hours). Planned Perth–London and Singapore–New York nonstop services were set to reshuffle the rankings."}

{"summary":"“Orange Is the New Black” Season 2 premieres June 6 on Netflix, a date revealed during the end credits of the “House of Cards” Season 2 finale. Laura Prepon will return as Alex for at least four episodes, and Lori Petty will join the cast."}

{"summary":"Pokémon CEO Tsunekazu Ishihara confirmed support for Nintendo’s NX and said it would change the meaning of home and handheld consoles—the clue supporting rumours of a hybrid device. Reports suggested a portable console with detachable controllers, but its design remained unconfirmed; release was planned for March 2017."}

{"summary":"Manohar Parrikar proposed all-women combat units across India’s Army, Navy and Air Force—the step the post praises as women’s empowerment. He also supported admitting women through the National Defence Academy and Sainik schools, while stressing that these changes should be gradual; the article describes proposals, not implemented policies."}

{"summary":"The intriguing characteristic is storytelling ability: studies of hundreds of undergraduates found that women rated men described as good storytellers as more attractive long-term partners and higher-status. Men did not show the same preference for female storytellers, and researchers have yet to test whether live storytelling produces the same effect."}

{"summary":"The Golden State Warriors are No. 1 in the NBA Power Rankings for the fourth straight week after nine consecutive wins. Memphis is their closest challenger, boasting a league-best 15 wins and just two losses; the Warriors, Grizzlies, Rockets, Blazers and Spurs make up the all-Western Conference top five."}

{"summary":"The overlooked workplace wellness issue is menopause: symptoms such as hot flashes, insomnia and concentration problems can affect job performance, while stressful or uncomfortable working conditions can worsen them. European guidelines urge employers to offer cooling, flexible schedules, bathroom breaks and supportive managers so women feel comfortable requesting accommodations."}

{"summary":"The morning habit being teased is meditation: the article recommends starting your day with a simple one-minute meditation exercise. It says meditation can improve focus and reduce stress, emphasizes that it needn’t be religious or follow one prescribed method, and promotes a free guided morning meditation MP3."}

{"summary":"Prince George wears shorts because of a centuries-old British aristocratic tradition that reserves long trousers for older boys and men. According to etiquette expert William Hanson, the custom reflects upper-class ideas about childhood and social status, and the royal family has followed it for generations."}

{"summary":"Robert Schwentke, director of “Red” and “R.I.P.D.,” will replace Neil Burger as director of “Insurgent,” the sequel to “Divergent.” Burger is not returning because of the tight production schedule, with “Insurgent” due in theaters March 20, 2015, roughly a year after the first film."}

{"summary":"The item is a leather jacket, which the article calls a timeless, versatile staple that works with jeans or dressier outfits. Choose a biker, motocross or bomber style to suit your budget, consider faux leather for a cheaper trial run, and avoid leather blazers."}

{"summary":"The “trick” is to reward journalism for meaningful engagement—such as readers finishing stories, sharing them or saying they loved them—instead of raw clicks. NPR’s Brian Boyer is developing Carebot to track these signals, hoping to reduce incentives for clickbait; whether it changes newsroom behavior remains unproven."}
{"summary":"Dino Morea’s celebrity lookalike is Scott Foley, who plays Jake on the American TV series Scandal. The article highlights the striking resemblance between the Bollywood actor and Foley."}

{"summary":"The gallery showcases shortlisted Sony World Photography Awards images selected from more than 220,000 entries, with the winner due to be announced on 20 April. Highlights include Mount Fuji during a marathon, panda handlers in panda suits, Italian beachgoers, Iranian mourners and portraits exploring racism, poverty and personal loss."}

{"summary":"Pokémon Go is introducing advertising through “sponsored locations,” where businesses pay to become destinations on the game’s virtual map to attract players and drive foot traffic. The article predicts backlash from users accustomed to ad-free gameplay."}

{"summary":"Traffic and social shares don’t prove people read your content: CoSchedule found only 10–20% of readers reached the bottom, with many stopping after 20–30%. Use heatmaps to assess engagement, put key information first, and improve readability with clear headings, short paragraphs, bullets, images, and mobile-friendly design."}

{"summary":"Republican policy intellectual Avik Roy predicts the GOP will collapse or be replaced because its base is driven by white nationalism rather than conservative principles—an increasingly untenable foundation in a diversifying America. He sees Trump as the culmination of that history and argues gradual reform cannot fix the party."}

{"summary":"A “perfect,” 100-carat emerald-cut diamond sold for $22.1 million at Sotheby’s in under three minutes, setting a New York auction record for a colorless diamond. The internally flawless stone went to an anonymous telephone bidder, within its estimated $19 million–$25 million price range."}

{"summary":"The article describes a school form allowing parents to exempt their children from reciting the Pledge of Allegiance—not requiring opposition to it. The headline teases a mother’s angry response, supposedly shown in a social-media photo, but the provided article text never reveals what she actually wrote or did."}
